newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks lower, investors wait-and-see. [CORRECTED 14:02 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks lower, investors wait-and-see. [CORRECTED 14:02 GMT]

text.p: The Jordanian bourse fell on Tuesday in weak demand as institutional and private investors kept to the sidelines awaiting cabinet approval of rules which open ownership of most listed stocks to foreigners.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell 0.06 percent (corrects measure of fall from points) to 161.02 points in trade worth just 608,012 dinars ($857,562).

Market sentiment remains subdued ahead of anticipated cabinet approval soon to implement a decision by a top investment body last week to scrap a 50 percent ceiling on foreign ownership. The ceiling would be maintained on mining, trade and construction stocks.

The move, expected at next Saturday's cabinet meeting, should jump-start the bourse which has seen foreign demand ebb after a bout of heavy buying in May which sent the bourse to its highest trading levels in over two years.
Dealers said brokers associated with foreign funds were picking up Jordan Cement Factories stock from the trading floor to meet a large foreign bloc order.
JOCM stock stood unchanged at 4.08 dinars after shares worth 178,407 dinars exchanged hands in the busiest stock on Tuesday.
In a market which otherwise lacked any significant buying orders, Arab Bank ended one dinar higher at 264 dinars but only 200 shares changed hands.
The bank rose sharply last week on expectation of a surge in demand once the cabinet approves the elimination of the foreign ownership ceiling recommendation.
Falling shares outnumbered gainers on Tuesday by 22 to seven, with another 14 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.24 percent to 80.51 points, 3.44 percent down from the start of the year.
